problem:
The position $x(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
x(t)={t}^{2}-10t-2,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary.

feedback.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=(t-3){e}^{t},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero. So first, we need to calculate the velocity function. We can do that by taking the derivative of the position function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-3){e}^{t}) \\  & ={e}^{t}+(t-3){e}^{t} \\  & =(t-2){e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m/s}.$ So, we set $v=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(t-2){e}^{t} & =0 \\ t-2 & =0 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary at $t=2\,\text{s}.$
